rules.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.32(1): all deductions in a salary period other than under s.27(1)(a) (absence), (f) (advances, loans, overpayments) and (j) (co-operative society) may not exceed 50% of the salary payable for that period — CPF contributions (s.27(1)(h)) count; s.32(2): the last salary on termination or completion of the contract is outside the limit. The independent per-instalment quarter caps of s.31(3) and (5) apply even on final salary; an excessive instalment is left wholly outstanding. See MOM Allowable salary deductions and JKB v JKC [2026] SGECT 11 paras.18–22 (https://www.elitigation.sg/gd/s/2026_SGECT_11). EA s.2 salary excludes travelling allowance, expense reimbursements, benefits in kind, gratuity and retrenchment benefits. Catalogue codes in basis_exempt_codes carry those classifications; customer-specific codes must be classified in the sealed settings. Salary overpayment and unearned-benefit recovery are outside s.31 instalment caps (MOM Allowable salary deductions). EA s.31(2): recovery of an advance is spread over no more than 12 months; the first scheduled instalment, including settled history, anchors the limit. EA ss.29–30: damage recovery is a one-time deduction limited to a quarter of one month salary; accepted accommodation and approved amenities/services share a quarter of salary-period salary, no more than their supplied value. These independent limits also apply on final pay. s.32(1) excludes consented registered-co-operative payments from its aggregate half. The damage limit applies per incident; the separate APPROVED_DAMAGE_RECOVERY class requires the Commissioner permission as evidence for the s.29(1) exception. The aggregate s.32 limit still applies. EA s.31(1): actual disbursed_on is required for an advance. If it was paid before employment, recovery starts only with the first completed salary period; pre-employment TRAVEL_ADVANCE is never recoverable from salary.

name: Rest-day work without who asked for it

rules.when: terms.work_classification == "EA_COVERED" && (employment.classification != "NON_EA" && ((terms.statutory_work_category != "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 4500.0) || (terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 2600.0)) && size(work.days.filter(d, d.day_type == "REST" && d.worked_hours > 0.0)) > 0 && !has(employee.facts.rest_day_work_requester))
rules.message: Rest-day work is recorded but not who asked for it (employee.facts.rest_day_work_requester): EA s.37 pays 1 or 2 days at the employer’s request, ½ or 1 at the employee’s. Record it and rebuild before paying.
rules.description: Employment Act 1968 s.37(2)–(3): the rest-day pay depends on who requested the work; the slip is held rather than paying nothing.

name: Rest-day work without normal daily hours

rules.when: terms.work_classification == "EA_COVERED" && (employment.classification != "NON_EA" && ((terms.statutory_work_category != "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 4500.0) || (terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 2600.0)) && size(work.days.filter(d, d.day_type == "REST" && d.worked_hours > 0.0)) > 0 && !((has(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours) ? double(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours) : size(work.days.filter(w, w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0)) > 0 ? double(first(work.days.filter(w, w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0).map(w, w.scheduled_hours))) : 0.0) > 0.0))
rules.message: Rest-day work is recorded but the normal daily hours are unknown (no employee.facts.normal_daily_hours and no planned working shift): EA s.37 pays by whether the work exceeded half of them. Record them and rebuild before paying.
rules.description: Employment Act 1968 s.37(2)–(3): half or more of the normal daily hours decides the rest-day pay; the slip is held rather than paying nothing.

name: Part-time holiday work without contracted weekly hours

rules.when: terms.employment_type == "PART_TIME" && !has(employee.facts.part_time_weekly_hours) && size(work.days.filter(d, has(d.holiday_kind) && d.holiday_kind in ["PUBLIC_HOLIDAY", "SUBSTITUTE"] && d.worked_hours > 0.0)) > 0
rules.message: A part-timer worked a public holiday but the contracted weekly hours (employee.facts.part_time_weekly_hours) are not recorded, so the hourly basic rate cannot be set. Record them and rebuild before paying.
rules.description: Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations: holiday work is paid at the hourly basic rate from the contracted hours; the slip is held rather than paying nothing.

name: Report a work incident to MOM

rules.description: Submit an incident report within ten days. For non-fatal employee light-duty accidents, open the case on the employer’s first notice; for fatal accidents, on the accident date; for a dangerous occurrence or a work-related public/self-employed fatality, on the occurrence date. Dangerous-occurrence and public/self-employed cases are duties of the workplace occupier. Select those cases only where the company is the occupier and the event meets MOM reportable criteria. No medical-leave entry is needed. Cross-reference any leave-triggered report to avoid filing the same incident twice.
rules.authority: Ministry of Manpower, Work-related accidents: what and when to report, employer/occupier and occupational-disease tables, read 2026-10-10: https://www.mom.gov.sg/workplace-safety-and-health/work-accident-reporting/what-and-when-to-report. WSH (Incident Reporting) and Work Injury Compensation Regulations. The current agency criteria are verified; direct legislation links were inaccessible (403).

name: Notify the Commissioner of a workplace incident

rules.description: Notify the Commissioner as soon as reasonably practicable for an employee work-related fatality, a reportable dangerous occurrence, or a work-related public/self-employed fatality or injury sent to hospital. The latter three cases are occupier duties. The case date is an operational prompt to act, not a statutory fixed-day deadline. The Commissioner notification is distinct from the ten-day incident report; public/self-employed hospital treatment here requires notification without inventing a ten-day report duty.

name: Immediately notify a subsequent death from work injury or disease

rules.description: If an employee subsequently dies from a work injury or disease, immediately notify the Commissioner. Open the case on learning the death, link the original incident and report, and act immediately; do not wait for a medical-leave entry or restart the original ten-day report period.

WSH (Incident Reporting) and Work Injury Compensation Regulations. The current agency criteria are verified; direct legislation links were inaccessible (403).

name: Report an employee occupational disease diagnosis

rules.description: As employer, submit an incident report within ten days of receiving the occupational-disease diagnosis. Open this case on that receipt date. Covers reportable diseases under WSHA or WICA; no leave entry is required. A doctor’s separate statutory report does not replace the employer report. This employer task does not assert the company is a platform operator or medical practitioner.
